universal_required: Category framing at the top: what a smart toilet is and exactly what Skyflex offers — the two models in the range (U6 and U7 Smartoilet) — so a researcher lands on a clear, honest picture of the range, not an implied deep catalogue.

A product spec / comparison block for the two SKUs (U6 vs U7): dimensions, key features (bidet wash, warm-air dryer, seat vs integrated suite, mount type, any UV/self-clean), and the commercial basis — sourced from each model's own live page, no invented specs.

The assigned primary keyword 'smart toilets melbourne' in the title tag, H1, and first paragraph as an exact match, with a product-accurate title tag and meta description; the same page is written to also capture the higher-volume head term 'smart toilets' (Melbourne and national SERPs share 9 of the top 10 domains, so one page serves both).

The commercial terms stated plainly in the first half: price-from where a live page shows one, or an explicit 'enquire / consultation' line where it does not, plus the supply basis — matching what the live product pages say.

A named business-identity passage — an H2 such as 'About Skyflex' (never 'Why Choose Us') carrying founder Christopher Mitsopoulos, established 2023, 100+ customers, and the 50% referral rate — in wording unique to this page.

An FAQ block answering the real buyer questions captured in research (cost, is-it-worth-it, disadvantages, power-outage behaviour, toilet-paper use, what-plumbers-recommend, and the power-point/electrical requirement) — sourced from the 11 real Google PAAs plus real Reddit/Whirlpool/OzBargain threads; no invented Q&A.
A clear next-step CTA matched to the commercial model (enquire / book a showroom viewing / add-to-cart only if the live page supports it).
cluster_specific_required: Present the range using the facet/comparison axes competitors actually expose — brand/model, product type (integrated suite vs bidet seat), mount type (floor vs wall), price, and dimensions — as an honest comparison scaffold for the two SKUs. Do NOT pad the page with placeholder or fabricated products to imitate a deep catalogue.

Compensate for the thin catalogue with education-led depth, since Google rewards a category page here: cover the category-level questions the SERP and forums reward — what a smart toilet does, realistic cost range, the disadvantages, the power-point/electrical requirement, and behaviour in a power outage — grounded in the 11 real PAAs and the real Reddit/Whirlpool/OzBargain threads captured in research. Never invent a statistic, review, or specification.

Honest positioning — this is a conversion/showcase page for an outdoor-living brand adding a bathroom category with NO topical authority in it. Do NOT write authority claims Skyflex has not earned ('leading smart toilet retailer', 'Australia's best smart toilets', years of bathroom expertise). Confine claims to what is true: the two models, their real specs, price, and any warranty the product's own page states.

The power-point / electrical-connection requirement and WELS/water rating (only where a product page states it) must be covered — the top real buyer concern from the forums; stating it builds trust and reduces mismatched-expectation returns.

Product-claim scoping: the 15-year warranty, the 'most affordable louvre roof' award, and the pergola USPs are for a different product line and MUST NOT appear on this smart-toilet page. Any warranty/price/spec claim here must come from the U6/U7 product pages or research bundle.
